page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfr6.3xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual server instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 12 dedicated vCPUs mapped from 6 physical Intel Xeon 8269CY processor cores with hyper-threading enabled. Operating at a clock speed of 3.1 GHz, the x86_64 architecture CPU includes a 35 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and AVX512_VNNI. The instance is configured with 96.0 GB of RAM, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or GPU accelerators, and it delivers a baseline network bandwidth of 4 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations place the ecs.hfr6.3xlarge consistently in the average performance tier. The single-core stress-ng CPU performance is recorded at 1435.7, while the multi-core score reaches 11480.59. Memory bandwidth tests show a read-only small block cached speed of 640.72 GB/sec, which drops to 72.14 GB/sec for uncached large blocks, alongside a write speed of 45.09 GB/sec. In application-specific workloads, the instance achieves a Redis SET throughput of 11.09 million operations per second and a static web serving throughput of 9.73 GB/sec. For language model processing, it handles 135M model text generation at 165.19 tokens per second, though performance degrades to a weak rating of 17.27 tokens per second for 7B model prompt processing.

Given its dedicated CPU allocation and high memory density, this instance offers qualitative cost efficiency for memory-bound workloads that do not require local NVMe storage or GPU acceleration. The absence of bundled local storage means users must rely on network-attached storage, which is a key architectural tradeoff to consider. The ecs.hfr6.3xlarge is suited for in-memory databases like Redis, caching layers, enterprise applications, and moderate data processing tasks that benefit from a 1:8 vCPU-to-RAM ratio.
